extracted.intended_audience: startup founders and early-stage startup teams (founders doing their own PR)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for founders on when and how to do PR and press for startups, including readiness checklists, story prioritization, pitching rules, interview prep, crisis communication, and pitfalls to avoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: PR is not a substitute for product
rubrics_metrics.description: PR is not a substitute for product
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes that press cannot replace having a working, valuable product; focus on product-market fit before heavy PR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founders should do PR themselves at first
rubrics_metrics.description: Founders should do PR themselves at first
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early-stage founders are expected to lead pitching and spokesperson duties rather than delegating immediately to agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth is the best PR strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Truth is the best PR strategy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be honest in pitches and public statements; avoid exaggeration or misleading claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build relationships, not transactions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach reporters and media contacts as long-term relationships (not one-off asks); invest in personalization and respect for their work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of coverage > quantity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize high-quality placements and accurate coverage over many low-value hits (avoid chasing vanity coverage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Product is working in production
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the readiness checklist items: ensure the product is actually shipping and usable before pitching; anti-pattern: PR before product is live.

rubrics_metrics.name: 10+ paying customers (or 1,000+ active users)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete numeric proof points to demonstrate traction and newsworthiness; used as a signal that the story may be ready for press.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder can articulate the problem clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: Founder can articulate the problem clearly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Founders should be able to explain the problem their product solves succinctly before doing PR; this improves pitch clarity and interview performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: You have data or proof points to share
rubrics_metrics.description: You have data or proof points to share
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare concrete metrics (revenue, users, growth) or case studies to support claims in pitches and press materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: You can spare time for media days
rubrics_metrics.description: You can spare time for media days
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Founders should ensure they have bandwidth to do interviews, follow-ups, and media preparation when coverage runs; don't launch PR if you can't support it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Series A+ funding (Tier 1)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classified as 'Always Worth PR' (Tier 1); high-priority story type that typically merits outreach and coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major customer wins (named) (Tier 1)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tier 1: Named, significant customer logos or contracts are considered high-value press events deserving outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisition or significant partnership (Tier 1)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tier 1: Mergers, acquisitions, or partnerships that materially change company trajectory are always PR-worthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry-defining data report (Tier 1)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tier 1: Publishing data or reports that influence industry discourse is high-value PR material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notable hire (if person is famous) (Tier 2)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tier 2: Hiring a well-known industry figure can be newsworthy; otherwise, minor hires are low priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major product launch with new capability (Tier 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Major product launch with new capability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tier 2: Large feature launches or product expansions that introduce new capabilities can merit PR; minor updates generally do not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis or controversy response (Tier 2)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tier 2: When responding to crises, proactive communication is often warranted; treat as higher-priority outreach to manage narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pivot announcement (Tier 2)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tier 2: Major strategic pivots that change business direction can be newsworthy, depending on scale and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor product updates (Tier 3)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tier 3: Avoid pitching small incremental changes as news; these are rarely worth press outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Junior hires (Tier 3)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tier 3: Non-notable hires should not be treated as press-worthy; focus on senior/notable hires only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vanity awards (Tier 3)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tier 3: Awards with little editorial weight or recognition are low-value and unlikely to gain meaningful coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic 'we hit milestone X' (Tier 3)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tier 3: Generic milestone announcements without compelling context or data tend to be ignored by press.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always pitch to one reporter at a time
rubrics_metrics.description: Always pitch to one reporter at a time
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitch exclusivity and one-on-one outreach increases rapport and respect; avoid mass-blasting the same pitch to many reporters simultaneously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalize based on their recent work
rubrics_metrics.description: Personalize based on their recent work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor each pitch to the reporter's beat and recent articles; reference past coverage to show relevance and preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer exclusive when possible
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offering an exclusive can increase the likelihood of a feature; use exclusives strategically and sparingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor embargoes religiously
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reporter grants an embargo, do not violate it; respecting embargoes builds trust and long-term relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't follow up more than once
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't follow up more than once
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit persistence to a single follow-up to avoid annoying reporters; excessive chasing harms relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3 key talking points memorized
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare and internalize three concise messages to return to during interviews; keeps coverage focused and consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1 anecdote ready for 'tell me a story'
rubrics_metrics.description: 1 anecdote ready for 'tell me a story'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have a short, human story or example that illustrates the company's mission or product impact; reporters often ask for narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific numbers ready (revenue, users, growth)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared with concrete metrics to substantiate claims; vagueness weakens credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honest about what you don't know
rubrics_metrics.description: Honest about what you don't know
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you lack information, say so rather than guessing; honesty preserves trust and reduces risk of being corrected publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid hype language
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steer clear of buzzwords and inflated claims; reporters prefer grounded, specific descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice with someone on the team first
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice with someone on the team first
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rehearse interviews internally to refine messaging and anticipate tough questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge within hours, not days (crisis)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a crisis, respond quickly to show accountability; delays exacerbate scrutiny and damage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific about what happened (crisis)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear facts about the incident rather than vague statements; specificity helps restore trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take responsibility, don't deflect (crisis)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Own mistakes where appropriate; deflection damages credibility and prolongs negative coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outline concrete corrective steps (crisis)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain what the company is doing to fix the issue and prevent recurrence; actionable commitments matter to reporters and stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update regularly during ongoing situation (crisis)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide periodic status updates as events unfold to keep stakeholders informed and show progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hiring expensive agency too early (what to skip)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid costly PR firms before you have product-market traction; founders should run PR initially to learn and save resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wire-only distribution (what to skip)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relying solely on wire services is discouraged; targeted outreach and relationships are preferred over mass distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vanity metrics in press releases (what to skip)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't highlight metrics that lack substance (e.g., unengaged users); focus on meaningful proof points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitching the same story to many reporters (what to skip)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitching the same story to many reporters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid simultaneous mass pitching; personalize and offer exclusives when appropriate instead of broadcasting the same pitch widely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press tours before product is ready (what to skip)
rubrics_metrics.description: Press tours before product is ready
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not invest time/money in press tours until product and team can support the resulting interest and coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product genuinely ready (Quality Rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of YC's explicit quality rubric: product must be real and ready before pursuing press; echoes 'product is working in production' readiness item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier 1 or 2 story type (Quality Rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality rubric requires that the story be Tier 1 or Tier 2 (not Tier 3) to justify PR effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder is spokesperson (Quality Rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: YC recommends the founder be the public face for press, especially early on; strengthens authenticity and messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalized pitches (Quality Rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the quality checks: pitches must be personalized to reporters, not boilerplate blasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive offered (Quality Rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offering an exclusive is listed in the quality rubric as a factor that increases the chance of coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honest, specific claims (Quality Rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims in press materials must be truthful and backed by specific data or proof points; avoids hype and vagueness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder prepared for interviews (Quality Rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Founders must be ready with talking points, anecdotes, and metrics prior to media engagement.
